records.kind: transactions with the bank's reserves prohibited by a foreign authority
records.summary: The Council of the European Union, by Regulation (EU) 2022/398 of 9 March 2022, inserted Article 1ja into Regulation (EC) No 765/2006 prohibiting all transactions related to the management of the reserves and assets of the Central Bank of Belarus, including transactions with anybody acting on its behalf or at its direction, with a derogation only where a transaction is strictly necessary for the financial stability of the Union or of a Member State. The recitals of the same regulation also prohibit the supply of euro denominated banknotes to Belarus, including to the Central Bank of Belarus. The EUR-Lex record of the act is marked 'In force'. Belarus's one existing record on this row is the dismissal of 18 July 2011, a different episode with different actors.
records.quote: Transactions related to the management of reserves as well as of assets of the Central Bank of Belarus
records.source_title: Council Regulation (EU) 2022/398 of 9 March 2022 amending Regulation (EC) No 765/2006 (EUR-Lex, English text, marked 'In force')

records.kind: central bank designated and its assets frozen by a foreign authority
records.summary: Council Decision 2012/122/CFSP of 27 February 2012 states in its recitals that 'restrictive measures should be imposed against the Central Bank of Syria', adds the Central Bank of Syria to the asset-freeze list in Annex I of Decision 2011/782/CFSP with the reason given as 'Providing financial support to the regime' and a date of listing of 27.2.2012, and inserts a new Article 8a prohibiting the sale, purchase, transportation or brokering of gold, precious metals and diamonds to, from or for the Central Bank of Syria. The text cited is the decision as adopted (the legislation.gov.uk copy of the EU instrument); the EU's Syria measures were later carried into further decisions, so this record is of the dated 2012 act and not of a measure asserted to be current. Syria's one existing record on this row is the 2002 statutory arrangement, a different episode.
records.quote: restrictive measures should be imposed against the Central Bank of Syria
records.source_title: Council Decision 2012/122/CFSP of 27 February 2012 amending Decision 2011/782/CFSP concerning restrictive measures against Syria (full text, Annex I)

records.kind: the bank objects in writing to a government bill
records.summary: The Banco de Portugal's formal written opinion (parecer), dated Lisbon, 13 February 2019, on the government's draft bill Projeto de Proposta de Lei n.o 575/2018 creating and regulating the Sistema Nacional de Supervisao Financeira, objects to the bill on independence grounds: it states that the bank's independent status is a necessary condition for its participation in the Eurosystem, that the intervention of the Inspecao-Geral de Financas provided for in the draft collides in a relevant way with the Banco de Portugal's status of independence, that its independence is also protected by the prohibition of monetary financing, and that removing functions from the bank could leave it unable to go on financing them, at possible cost to the market, to supervised entities or to taxpayers. This is a government bill the bank opposed in writing, not a reform the bank sought. Portugal's one existing record on this row is the 12 April 2016 pressure episode, different actors and a different year. The document is in Portuguese and about 324,000 characters; the opinion's objections quoted here are in its first 100,000 characters, which is the part read.
records.source_title: Banco de Portugal, Parecer do Banco de Portugal sobre o projeto de proposta de lei que cria e regula o Sistema Nacional de Supervisao Financeira (13 February 2019)

records.kind: arrest and detention of the bank's national director
records.summary: Financial Afrik reports that on Tuesday 31 October 2023 Maman Laouali Abdou Rafa, the BCEAO's Directeur National for Niger, was taken into custody and had not reappeared by the article's publication on 3 November 2023, that no reason had been given, that the BCEAO said it was still waiting to be told why he was detained and had referred the matter to its lawyers, and that he had already been detained once in August and summoned several times by the external security service. The report attributes the arrest to the junta in its headline; the body of the article does not name the body that carried it out, and this record does not either. Not a duplicate: Niger's existing event is the January 2011 forced resignation of the BCEAO governor, expanded into every WAEMU member.
records.status_note: Filed as an event, not a case: the page states no allegation of any specific conduct against him, so there is nothing for the corruption row to record. Trade press, so weak.
records.source_title: Niger : la junte arrete le directeur national de la BCEAO sans explications (Financial Afrik, 3 November 2023)

records.summary: Financial Afrik reports that Anouar Mahamat Hassan, BEAC's national director for Chad, was suspended immediately following a request made to BEAC by Chad's Minister of Economy and Finance, Tahir Hamid Ngulin, who said he acted conformement aux textes, and that the letter was sent on 4 May; the page prints only le 4 mai dernier, so the year 2021 here comes from the article's own publication date of 14 May 2021 and not from a date printed in the text. The page gives no official reason for the suspension, reports a rumour that he was judged peu favorable au Conseil militaire de la transition and reports other unnamed sources saying the matter concerns relations between Chad and the central bank. Not a duplicate: Chad's existing event is the October 2009 dismissal of the BEAC governor, expanded into every CEMAC member.
records.status_note: Filed as an event, not a case: the page states no allegation of misconduct, so nothing belongs on the corruption row. The event qualifies because a state organ, the Chadian finance ministry, acted against the central bank's national leadership in the country. Trade press, so weak.
records.source_title: Tchad : suspension du frere de Moussa Faki Mahamat, directeur national pour la BEAC (Financial Afrik, 14 May 2021)

blanks.note: Candidate second episode: the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Economic Objective) Amendment Bill, passed under urgency in December 2023, which removed the employment objective from the bank's statutory mandate (RNZ, 13 December 2023, 'Reserve Bank dual mandate repeal passes through Parliament'). Refused without opening the article because the same search returned an interest.co.nz headline stating that Governor Adrian Orr said the central bank had itself recommended an inflation-only objective. Under the round 70 and 71 rule a reform the bank asked for or agreed to is not this row, and the question of whether the bank sought it has to be settled before filing. Next round: open interest.co.nz/public-policy/125457 and the Treasury information release 'Reserve Bank dual mandate' to see what the bank advised; if the bank opposed or was not consulted, this is a clean second record for New Zealand.

Candidate: removal of the SAMA governor by royal decree. Arabian Business, 'Saudi Arabia's King Salman orders removal of central bank governor', read in full: it states only that 'Fahad Al Mubarak was removed from his post following a royal decree, state-run press agency SPA said' and that a further royal decree named Ayman Alsayari as the new head, with immediate effect. The page carries no date for the order and gives no reason for the removal, so it fails both this round's rule that every date must be on the cited page and the row's rule against an unexplained early exit. Next round: the SPA royal-order text or Saudi Gazette article 629500, which names Al-Sayari.

Candidate: replacement of Bank of the Lao PDR governor Sonexay Sitphaxay by Bounleua Sinxayvoravong, approved by the Lao National Assembly on Monday 20 June 2022 during the kip crisis (RFA, 'Laos shuffles top Cabinet posts amid economic slowdown', 22 June 2022, read in full). The article gives no reason for the governor change and ties only the wider cabinet reshuffle to the economic crisis; it does not state criticism of the governor or any pressure. An appointment or an unexplained exit is not this row. Next round: the Vientiane Times and kpl.gov.la National Assembly reports of that session, which may record what was said about the bank.

Turkmenistan's one record is the January 2014 dismissal. Tried the official route for a second: the Turkmen MFA's own news feed (Embassy of Turkmenistan in Kabul). Page /en/news/19607, 'The President of Turkmenistan severely reprimands a number of officials', read in full - the five officials severely reprimanded are the Minister and a Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Water Industry, the Chairman of the State Customs Service, the Chairman of the Turkmenhimiya State Concern and the Dashoguz velayat hyakim; the Central Bank chairman is not among them, and the page prints only '12 Oct' with no year. Page /en/news/82584, 'OFFICIAL NEWS' (9 Jul), read in full - it records the appointment of Central Bank chairman Gadyrgeldi Mushshikov as managing director for the IMF and the Asian Development Bank, which is an appointment, not an action against the bank. Trend.az article 2466746, 'Heads of Central Bank, commodity exchange reprimanded in Turkmenistan', was not opened for want of budget and is the single best next lead for this country.

Candidate: US restrictions on dollar flows through the Central Bank of Iraq. A search returned The National, 20 July 2023, 'US bars 14 Iraqi banks from dollar transactions', and related Middle East Policy Council and Iraqi Economists Network pieces. Not filed and not opened: in every description the subject of the action is fourteen commercial banks and the Central Bank of Iraq is the channel and supervisor, which under the round 72 rule makes the bank the counterparty rather than the subject. The narrower candidate worth one fetch next round is the New York Fed's imposition of transfer controls on the CBI's own dollar account in November 2022, which would be an action on the bank itself.

Searched for a second Guyanese episode ('Bank of Guyana governor sent on leave government 2020'). Every result is an appointment or a routine supervisory story: centralbanking's 2014 appointment of Gobind Ganga, Stabroek News of 3 December 2014 confirming him, the Bank of Guyana's own governor profile page, Guyana Chronicle on new governor and deputy governor appointments, and the Bank of Guyana half-year report 2020. No source reports a removal, a suspension or pressure on the bank. Guyana's one record stays the 1998 statutory arrangement over exchange-rate policy.

Shape finding for the next round, from this round's yield. The richest unworked family on this row is a foreign state organ acting on a central bank or its leadership - the shape the map already carries for Afghanistan. It produced three of this round's five records (Belarus, Syria, Zimbabwe) from primary documents at EUR-Lex, legislation.gov.uk and govinfo, each of which states the act, the date and the reason on the page. Within this assignment that family now looks exhausted: the other EU and US designations of a central bank by name (Iran, Russia, Libya, North Korea) are countries not on this list, and Cuba was not filed because the Cuban Assets Control Regulations block Cuban government property generally without naming the central bank. The second-richest family is the central bank's own written objection to a government bill, which produced the Portugal record; the ECB's CON opinions remain the repeatable form of it for every EU country here, but ecb.europa.eu HTML is robots-disallowed and the lagen.nu mirror of the opinions is robots-disallowed too, so an opinion has to be reached either through a national bank's own site, as Portugal's was, or through an /ecb/legal/pdf/ URL returned by a search.
